surface_form_payload.question_text: Assign the frequency, severity, and qualitative risk categories independently.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent is to keep V-001 liquid within its control band so gas leaves liquid-free. The deviation is Level/More (CASE-02, CASE-03). FREQUENCY: The four causes in CASE-04 (spurious SDV-101/SDV-102 closure, LV-101/LV-102 failing closed) are credible single failures that close the liquid outlet path, so a high-level demand is expected during facility life. Two existing layers in CASE-06, LAH-102 and LAHH-103, each close SDV-30010 and are intended to act before flooding. Credit is limited because both share SDV-30010 as final element, and sensor independence and response time are undocumented. Escalation to flooding/carryover is therefore rated C (Casual), not A/B, and not E. SEVERITY: The stated consequences (CASE-05) are flooding, liquid carryover to the gas line and treatment unit, possible generator damage, unit shutdown and production loss. These are asset and business impacts. No injury, loss of containment, fire/explosion or environmental release is stated, so severity is III (Average). RISK: Matrix III/C gives M. M is robust: it also results from III/B-D, IV/A-C, and II/C-E for the shutdown/production-loss outcome. ANCHOR: The preliminary E/V/H is rejected. V has no consequence basis in the packet. E disregards the two level safeguards and could at most describe the initiating demand, whose safeguarded outcome is lower severity. RECOMMENDATIONS: Verify that LAH-102/LAHH-103 sensors are independent of the LV-101/LV-102 control loops. Confirm SDV-30010 closure time against liquid rise time from LAHH to carryover. Define SDV-30010 proof testing. Evaluate protection of the generator gas supply against liquid carryover. SUBJECTIVE PROBABILITY (judgment aid only, not a matrix input): about 15% that flooding with carryover occurs at least once over the facility operating life.
safeguards_considered: LAHH-103 high-high level with closing action of SDV-30010: credited as the primary protective layer; independence and response time are unverified.
LAH-102 high level with closing action of SDV-30010: credited only partially because it shares SDV-30010 with LAHH-103, so a common-cause failure limits the combined credit.
No credit taken for operator intervention, relief devices, downstream liquid knock-out or generator protections, because none are listed in the packet.

supporting_evidence.relevance: Defines the node scope: V-001 and associated lines.
The Level/More guideword establishes the high-level deviation being assessed.
The deviation is more liquid in V-001, which is the scenario whose frequency and severity are rated.
Four credible single-failure causes (spurious SDV-101/SDV-102 closure, LV-101/LV-102 failing closed) make a high-level demand expected during facility life, supporting a frequency above Remote.

The consequences are flooding, carryover, possible generator damage, shutdown and production loss. These are asset and business impacts with no injury, loss of containment or environmental harm stated, which supports severity III and rules out V.

LAH-102 and LAHH-103 both close SDV-30010, lowering the likelihood of escalation to flooding/carryover. Their shared final element limits the credit, supporting C rather than A/B, and argues against E.

uncertainty_notes: The packet gives no quantitative frequency bands, failure rates, demand history or operating data. Frequency C is an engineering judgment.

The design intent (normal level band, liquid-free gas outlet) is inferred from the separator function. Level set points, liquid hold-up between LAH/LAHH and flooding, and level ranges are not provided.

The packet does not state whether frequency is rated before or after safeguards. This rating credits the existing safeguards. Unmitigated, the initiating high-level demand could be D-E, but the outcome when SDV-30010 closes appears to be mainly shutdown and production loss, rated about II, which is still M.

LAH-102 and LAHH-103 share SDV-30010 as their final element. The packet does not show whether their level sensors are independent of the LV-101/LV-102 control loops. SDV-30010 closure time and proof-test status are also unknown.
The function and location of SDV-30010 are not described in the packet. It is presumed to stop liquid inflow to V-001.

The extent of possible generator damage, repair duration, and whether loss of the generators affects safety-critical power are unknown. If judged severe, severity IV could be argued: IV/C is still M, but IV/D would be H.
No personnel injury, loss of containment, fire/explosion or environmental consequence is stated, and none was assumed. Severity V would require evidence of such outcomes.

The subjective probability is a labeled judgment aid only. It means the probability of at least one flooding/carryover event over the facility operating life. It is not derived from packet data and is not a matrix input.
